# Keyboard sound lab.

Press any key on your real keyboard — or click the on-screen one — to hear what a mechanical keyboard sounds like. Eight switch packs, recorded from physical boards. Free, no download.

100% freeNo signupNothing recorded

Live sound studioTYPE SOMETHING

Choose a sound

Press any key to start

Quick start

## Three steps to maximum thock.

1. Turn your volume up and put headphones on if you are somewhere quiet.
2. Type normally. Every key you press on your physical keyboard triggers a sample, so type a full sentence rather than tapping one key — the rhythm is most of the effect.
3. Switch packs using the buttons above and type the same sentence again to compare them properly.

Meet the lineup [...] Alpine Pop
:   Light, glassy, and quick — a bright linear with a poppy top note on every press. No click, no bump, just a lively patter that stays crisp at speed.

Onyx Glide
:   A smooth, deep linear with the edges rounded off. Presses land low and even, closer to a soft drum than a click — a calm sound for long sessions.

Glacier Glide
:   Bright and clean without being clicky. A slick linear with a cool, glassy clack — lighter than the thock packs, gentler than a true click.

Cream Clack
:   Full and rounded with a satisfying clack on the bottom-out. The plushest-sounding pack of the set — deep like a thock, but with more snap to it.

Hear each switch on a page of its own:

Cherry MX Blue Clicky Cherry MX Brown Tactile Cherry MX Red Linear Cherry MX Black Linear [...] Or hear two switches head to head:

Blue vs Brown Clicky vs Tactile Red vs Brown Linear vs Tactile Red vs Black Linear vs Linear Blue vs Red Clicky vs Linear Blue vs Black Clicky vs Linear Brown vs Black Tactile vs Linear

Each pack holds several samples for the same key, picked at random on every press, with a small pitch variation on top. That is what stops a mechanical keyboard from sounding like a machine gun of one identical click — and it is why the space bar and return key sound distinct from the letters.

## Build a custom keyboard, then hear it

The builder turns this into a custom keyboard simulator. Pick from 17 layouts including Alice and ortholinear, choose a keycap profile, apply a colorway or paint individual keys, import your own arrangement from keyboard-layout-editor, then share the result as a link or export it as an image. Pair it with the switch you were just listening to and you have the look and the sound settled before ordering anything.

## Typing sounds and hardware testing [...] Design a board: layout, colorway, per-key paint, then share it or price the parts. ## Typing test

WPM and accuracy with switch sounds on, for QWERTY, Dvorak or Colemak.

## What this keyboard simulator does

This is an online keyboard simulator: a browser tool that reproduces how a real mechanical keyboard looks and sounds while you type. Choose a switch from the menu, then type on your own keyboard or tap the on-screen keys. Every keystroke plays that switch's press and release sound, and the matching key animates as it actuates.
